comparison: Perfect agreement on computational binding predictions (C84-C93). Both evaluations support the molecular dynamics simulations and binding mode predictions. OpenEval notes these require experimental validation, while peer reviewers praise the 'elegant' in silico modeling approach and note it is 'better described' in revision.

Perfect agreement on structure-activity relationship analysis (C130-C132). Both evaluations accept the chemical analysis and speculation about structural features. OpenEval explicitly notes these are 'reasonable speculation,' while peer reviewers implicitly accept by not questioning the structural explanations.

Strong agreement on in vivo zebrafish validation (C102-C112). Both evaluations support the findings on tumor size and dissemination. OpenEval notes C113 is 'appropriately cautious' speculation, while peer reviewers explicitly state 'studies in mammalian model systems are naturally needed in the future,' indicating acceptance with caveats about further validation needed.

Strong agreement on cell migration and polarization effects (C76-C83). Both evaluations support the actin polymerization, cell polarization, and migration data. Peer reviewers emphasize this selective targeting as a key strength enabling 'selective targeting of processes dependent upon cell polarisation and chemotaxis.'

Strong agreement on mutagenesis validation (C94-C99). Both evaluations support the experimental validation of computational predictions through site-directed mutagenesis. Peer reviewers note this as part of 'additional data that better illustrates the unique features of the new antagonist.'

Strong agreement on nanoclustering findings (C59-C63). Both evaluations support the SPT-TIRF data showing effects on receptor nanoclustering. OpenEval notes the term 'negative allosteric modulator' requires additional validation, while peer reviewers emphasize this as a core finding that 'abolishes ligand-induced CXCR4 receptor nanoclustering.'

Agreement on ligand binding preservation (C68-C70). Both evaluations support that compounds spare CXCL12 binding. Peer reviewers identify this as a 'key unique feature' distinguishing these compounds from traditional antagonists.

Agreement on selective signaling effects (C71-C73). Both evaluations support the selective inhibition profile sparing cAMP inhibition. Peer reviewers emphasize this enables 'selective targeting' without impacting all signaling effects, which OpenEval describes as 'a clear functional profile.'

Agreement on screening methodology and compound selection (C49-C58). Both evaluations support the virtual screening approach and compound validation. OpenEval provides detailed assessment of methodology, while peer reviewers praise the 'elegant modelling driven approach' and acceptance of AGR1.131 as appropriate control.

Agreement on computational screening methodology (C49-C52). Both evaluations support the virtual screening approach. OpenEval describes methodology as 'clearly described,' while peer reviewers note modeling work is 'better described' in revision and 'elegantly utilizes in silico drug modelling.'

Agreement on background literature (C1-C37). Both evaluations accept the cited background establishing scientific context. OpenEval notes these are 'accurately cited' literature claims, while peer reviewers implicitly accept by affirming the work's importance and not questioning the rationale.

Agreement on prior mechanistic work (C4-C6, C38-C48). Both evaluations accept the background on TMV-TMVI cleft targeting rationale.
